claims.text: A 57-year-old man without known comorbidities or risk factors for venous thromboembolism came to the emergency room with mild dyspnea and persistent right lower limb edema that began about a month earlier, with 3 days of fever and shivering. On examination he was afebrile, in good general health and dyspneic in room air, with normal auscultation, right leg edema, white blood count 12,150 without left shift, hematocrit 41%, and normal CK-MB, electrolytes, urea and creatinine.
